name: windows-execution-profile
purpose: Defines the Windows-specific execution structure for running the agent platform as local installable desktop software, from developer launch through signed installer distribution.

reader_guide.summary: Use this profile before claiming that the platform can run on Windows, adding Tauri/Electron installer code, launching local agents or CLIs from the desktop shell, or preparing MSI, NSIS, or MSIX releases.
how_to_read: Read execution_levels to distinguish developer launch, internal installer testing, and public signed distribution.
Read process_model before launching Python agents, local services, or external AI coding CLIs from a desktop app.
Read bundle_and_distribution_targets before choosing MSI, NSIS setup exe, or MSIX.
Read signing_requirements before public download, enterprise deployment, or Microsoft Store distribution claims.
Read smoke_tests before calling a Windows build runnable or release-ready.
update_triggers: The Windows desktop shell framework changes.
Tauri, Electron, Wails, or Windows packaging dependencies are installed.
The app starts launching Python agents, local services, file watchers, or external CLIs.
Windows installer format, code signing, WebView2, update, uninstall, or smoke-test behavior changes.
A Windows install, uninstall, SmartScreen, WebView2, or first-run smoke test fails.

structure_rules.rule: A developer-local Windows launch may be unsigned, but a public download or enterprise installer must have a documented code-signing strategy and install/uninstall smoke tests.
structure_rules.reason: Windows trust, SmartScreen, enterprise deployment, and update expectations differ from local developer runs.

structure_rules.rule: The Windows app owns the user entry point, while agent-platform remains the Python-first local platform layer behind a documented service, sidecar, or command boundary.
structure_rules.reason: The user should install and open one app, but platform internals must remain maintainable and testable.

structure_rules.rule: The Windows app must not scan arbitrary folders before the user selects or creates a workspace and sees what will be indexed or executed.
structure_rules.reason: Installable software needs a stronger privacy boundary than a repository-local script.

structure_rules.rule: Missing Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, GitHub CLI, package managers, or deployment CLIs must disable only the related capability and show setup guidance.
structure_rules.reason: The Windows app should open and show useful history/agents even before every optional CLI is configured.

structure_rules.rule: Auto-update is not enabled until artifacts, manifests, signatures, rollback behavior, and failure recovery are documented and smoke-tested on Windows.
structure_rules.reason: A broken update path can make local automation software harder to trust than manual workflows.

execution_levels.label: Developer local run
execution_levels.meaning: Run the desktop UI and platform from the repository on a developer Windows PC or VM.

execution_levels.label: Internal test installer
execution_levels.meaning: A packaged installer used for local or trusted internal testing.
allowed_artifacts: unsigned or test-signed NSIS setup exe
test-signed MSIX only when MSIX behavior is under review

execution_levels.label: Public signed distribution
execution_levels.meaning: A normal user can download, install, open, update, and uninstall the app without opaque security workarounds.
allowed_artifacts: signed MSIX only if Microsoft Store or enterprise deployment is selected

process_model.recommended_initial_shape: Tauri-first Windows desktop shell wrapping workspace-monitor output, with agent-platform invoked through a documented local service or sidecar only after the service boundary is specified.
process_model.ui_process: Desktop shell presents workspace-monitor as the first UI and adds native dialogs only where Windows file/workspace selection or permissions need native behavior.
process_model.agent_process: Python agent-platform remains outside renderer code. It is launched later as a sidecar, local service, or explicit command boundary with lifecycle cleanup and logs.
process_model.data_process: Repository documents and generated snapshots are read only from user-selected workspace paths.
process_model.cli_process: External CLIs run only through adapter contracts with allowlisted commands, timeouts, output redaction, and capability_missing fallback.
process_model.background_process_policy: No file watcher, local daemon, or queue starts silently before the user selects a workspace and the app records lifecycle cleanup.

owns: dashboard, history, docs, agents, source viewer, and decision inbox UI surfaces
research, planning, evaluation, config checks, and governance validators
tool-specific command invocation under explicit adapter contracts

bundle_and_distribution_targets.purpose: Primary Windows installer candidate when standard enterprise-friendly installer behavior is needed.
bundle_and_distribution_targets.notes: Tauri documents MSI creation through WiX and notes that MSI creation requires Windows.

bundle_and_distribution_targets.purpose: Primary Windows setup executable candidate for user-friendly direct downloads and cross-compilation experiments.
Use when Microsoft Store, enterprise MSIX deployment, or app-container package semantics are explicitly selected.

signing_requirements.secret_policy: Windows signing certificates, private keys, account credentials, and update private keys must be injected through CI secrets, OS certificate store, hardware token, or user-provided runtime input; they must not be committed.
signing_requirements.test_signing_policy: Self-signed or test certificates are acceptable only for internal testing and must not be described as public distribution-ready.

webview2_strategy.initial_policy: Use the Tauri default WebView2 installer behavior until offline installation becomes a real user requirement.
webview2_strategy.offline_policy: Only bundle or pin WebView2 runtime files after installer size, patch cadence, offline-user need, and support burden are reviewed.
webview2_strategy.smoke_test: Confirm Windows 10/11 target machines can open the app with the selected WebView2 mode.

permissions.notes: Use native folder picker or explicit workspace path. Do not scan home directories by default.
Needed only for update checks, web research, notifications, or remote services; document endpoint class before release.
All CLI execution must go through adapter contracts and visible user consent.
Slack, Discord, Teams, and OS notifications remain optional capabilities.

update_strategy.tauri_path: Use Tauri updater only after update server or static manifest hosting, update signing keys, rollback policy, and failure UI are documented.
update_strategy.manual_update_fallback: Before auto-update, provide versioned downloads and explicit migration notes.
update_strategy.windows_specific_warning: Do not enable update behavior until MSI/NSIS/MSIX replacement, uninstall, and rollback behavior are tested on a clean Windows account.

smoke_tests.check: Open local UI from a selected workspace and verify history, docs, agent catalog, and source viewer render.
Install/open the app on a clean Windows 11 account without developer repository state.
Confirm the app asks for a workspace before indexing or running commands.
Remove or hide optional CLIs and verify only related capabilities are disabled.
Uninstall the app and verify app files are removed while the user-selected workspace is not deleted without explicit consent.
Download and install the signed artifact on a separate Windows machine or clean VM and verify launch without opaque trust workarounds.
Simulate update unavailable, bad manifest, and rollback paths before enabling auto-update.

release_gates: Framework decision record comparing Tauri, Electron, Wails, and native packaging remains current.
Project-local dependency installation audit exists if desktop dependencies are installed.
Windows app process model and sidecar/local-service lifecycle are documented.
Code-signing certificate strategy, MSIX signing needs, and SmartScreen plan are complete.
No secrets or private repository snapshots are bundled.
Workspace boundary, optional CLI degradation, install, uninstall, and clean-account smoke tests pass.
Update, rollback, uninstall, and failure recovery are documented and tested before public release.

planned_commands.command: npm run tauri:build on a Windows build host after Rust, Node, Tauri CLI, and signing prerequisites are installed and audited.
To be defined after certificate strategy, CI secrets, and installer target are selected.
